title: Your first robot factory
intro: Build an offline robot factory from ordered instructions. Start with one fixed pickup fixture and one fixed destination. Pair roles: driver edits; observer predicts and checks; swap halfway. Only the instructor enables supervised hardware.
evidence_rule: Simulation, paper, reports and measured physical outcomes are separate evidence. Never claim a grasp or placement from a command log alone. Unknown or stale observations require pause and inspection.

missions.title: Make a short conveyor story
missions.goal: Put instructions in order and repeat a small section.
hints: Read from the top connection down.
Repeat repeats every block inside it; start with a message.
missions.worked_example: Ready → dispense → belt to pickup endpoint → inspect. In simulation each command changes a model; no physical object is verified.
missions.predict: Which message appears first? Where should the object model stop?
missions.change: Change Ready to your pair name. Add repeat 2 around a message, then around one tested short sequence.
missions.run: Open local Blockly simulation; select this mission; run the starter once. Use STOP and Reset before a different test. Save your workspace.
missions.observe: Read the command log and model state. Compare the repeated messages with your prediction.
missions.explain: Why do instruction order and a stopped belt matter before pickup?
missions.success: Your pair can trace the order, predict a repeat count and explain one corrected sequence.
missions.extension: Try an intentionally wrong order in simulation and explain the result.
missions.offline_route: Draw each instruction on paper and move a paper object only when its instruction runs.

missions.title: Separate the object from its report

else.message: Other or unknown: pause and inspect

hints: Compare actual and reported columns one row at a time.
A known word is still only a report.
missions.worked_example: An actual blue brick can have a missing report. An actual red brick can be reported blue. Both need inspection.
missions.predict: Which of the three reports is missing? Which disagrees with the labelled object?
missions.change: Change one report to None; then change one known report to a wrong known color.
missions.run: Run the short Python example or trace its three rows on paper. Compare the real labelled photo with a deliberately changed report.
missions.observe: Record actual object, reported label and your decision separately. None means missing, never zero or proof of empty space.
missions.explain: Why can a fresh color label still be wrong? What evidence would justify continuing?
missions.success: You identify one missing and one wrong report and choose pause/inspect for uncertainty.
missions.extension: Test unfamiliar green without adding a rule.
missions.offline_route: Use the supplied real photo and handwritten report cards; no camera or website is needed.

missions.title: Change a name and a number
missions.goal: Read and edit a short Python program before sharing the same program representation with blocks.

starter.message: Change a name and a number

hints: Quotes surround text; do not quote the number.
Four spaces keep print inside the loop.
missions.worked_example: TEAM stores text in quotes. REPEATS stores a number. print shows text. The indented line runs once for each number.
missions.predict: What greeting and how many object lines will appear?
missions.change: Change TEAM, predict, run. Then change REPEATS to 2, predict, run. Keep indentation.
missions.run: Open the Student notebook, save a pair copy and run cells from the top with Shift+Enter. Run the shared Program example in simulation.
missions.observe: Count output lines and compare the shared Python program JSON with the Blockly exported JSON.
missions.explain: Which edit changed text? Which changed how often a line ran? What stayed in the same order?
missions.success: Both partners make one edit and explain it; shared commands are validated before execution.
missions.extension: Change a wait or message in both Python and Blockly and compare command traces.
missions.offline_route: Run exercises/01_python.py using the prepared Python or trace it on paper. No package downloads.

missions.title: Watch teach inspect return replay
missions.goal: Understand that a recorded stroke needs validated start/end poses and explicit jaw state.
hints: A recording stores movement; it does not plan a safe approach from every pose.
A screen model can match commands while a physical object slips.
missions.worked_example: Leader 10°, follower 30°, leader now 15° gives relative request 35°. A request and a measured result are different.
missions.predict: Will a replay start safely from any pose? What if the jaw state changed?
missions.change: Ask the instructor to change one invented angle; predict before rerunning. Learners do not change physical modes.
missions.run: Watch instructor: teach a short empty stroke, stop recording, inspect metadata and path, return safely to its validated start, then replay separately.
missions.observe: Name start pose, endpoint, jaw state, identity/calibration and validity evidence. An invented demo recording is never a student-taught physical skill.
missions.explain: Why must teaching and playback be separate runs? Why does a changed robot or calibration require reteaching?
missions.success: You can say teach → inspect/validate → return to start → replay, and point to STOP.
missions.extension: Predict a relative versus absolute joint request.
missions.offline_route: Use the invented joint example and paper start/end diagrams. Label evidence DEMO.

missions.title: Explore three stations
missions.goal: Connect observations, instructions and the robot model.
hints: The twin is a model updated from a stream.
Use the same short sequence at the offline table.
missions.worked_example: Three pairs rotate through arm/twin observation, conveyor/observation sequencing, and offline Blockly/Python preparation.
missions.predict: At your current station, predict one direction, report or sequence before the instructor or simulator acts.
missions.change: Change only one paper angle, report or message; switch driver and observer halfway.
missions.run: Each slot is 15 minutes: 2 predict, 7 change/run, 4 observe/explain, 2 save and transition. Use the rotation table.
missions.observe: Arm: compare measured joint and twin when available. Conveyor: inspect stopped fixture/report. Offline: compare ordered traces. Label each evidence source.
missions.explain: Which part measures, decides or acts? What can your evidence establish?
missions.success: Every pair completes all three positions with one recorded prediction and evidence statement per position.
missions.extension: Compare a fresh report with a stale one without guessing missing values.
missions.offline_route: All three positions have photo, paper and simulation versions; record DEMO/OFFLINE if no measured stream.

missions.title: Dispense carry pick and place
missions.goal: Assemble the supervised fixed pickup to fixed destination sequence.
hints: Stop the conveyor before the arm approaches.
Start/end poses and jaw state of adjacent taught strokes must agree.
missions.worked_example: EV3 dispense → conveyor to pickup fixture and stop → named taught skill fixed_pick_place. That skill binds validated approach/open, calibrated grasp, lift/transfer, release and return phases. Missing or uncommissioned qualification blocks physical execution; simulation labels every transfer synthetic.
missions.predict: Where must the object and arm be before each next step? What should stop the run?
missions.change: First reorder paper cards. In simulation use pick_place_recording named fixed_pick_place and change one message or delay. Physical execution requires instructor-validated phase recordings, measured jaw calibration and the qualification manifest; missing evidence is a blocking result.
missions.run: Rotate: supervised integration, offline trace/rehearsal, failure/evidence desk. Each 15-minute slot includes 2 minutes transition. Run dispense, conveyor/stop and the named fixed_pick_place skill only through the existing shared endpoint. Instructor alone enables a qualified physical run; otherwise complete explicit synthetic simulation.
missions.observe: Record dispense, stopped fixture arrival, grasp, lift, placement/release and return separately. A completed command does not prove object transfer.
missions.explain: Which observation supports each claimed step? Which step remains unverified?
missions.success: Your pair explains the full fixed-fixture sequence and records honest per-step evidence. Physical completion requires observed object transfer; offline completion is labelled rehearsal.
missions.extension: After the core succeeds, discuss color-dependent destinations as separately validated taught skills.
missions.offline_route: Use the same fixed pickup/drop paper layout and named-skill simulation. Its grasp/lift/release outcomes are synthetic assumptions with physical_evidence false. Missing recordings or qualification means physical execution remains incomplete.

missions.title: Find one failure and test a repair
missions.goal: Use a controlled change and evidence to improve a sequence.
hints: Choose one input so cause and effect stay clear.
A successful run alone cannot identify a wrong known report.
missions.worked_example: A missing fixture observation pauses the sequence after one inspected object. Fix the observation path before retrying.
missions.predict: What happens when the middle report is None?
missions.change: Test one failure: missing report, wrong order, missing recording or STOP. Change one cause only and reset.
missions.run: Reproduce in simulation or paper; record expected versus actual. Repair and rerun the same input.
missions.observe: Capture the failure message, stopped state and repaired trace. No physical fault injection by learners.
missions.explain: Did your test detect the problem? What could still fail on hardware?
missions.success: You show a failing prediction, one repair and a repeated check with its limits.
missions.extension: Use the optional color-routing example with three reds and one blue to expose swapped rules.
missions.offline_route: All failures can be traced with paper command/report cards.

missions.title: Show one prediction and result
missions.goal: Explain what your program did and what the evidence cannot prove.
hints: Read your prediction before the result.
A trace supports instruction order, not physical arrival.
missions.worked_example: Pair A shows prediction, one change, observed result and one limit; then pairs B and C follow.
missions.predict: Which single output best supports your claim?
missions.change: Shorten your demonstration to one change and one observation.
missions.run: Use 1 minute preparation, 3 demonstrations of 2 minutes, 3 minutes shared reflection. Both partners speak.
missions.observe: Show saved trace, worksheet or observed supervised step; label simulation, paper or physical.
missions.explain: Name one next test that would increase confidence.
missions.success: All three pairs demonstrate and state a specific limitation.
missions.extension: Explain how a wrong known color differs from a missing report.
missions.offline_route: Present the worksheet and paper trace.

observation.code:
ACTUAL = ["red", "blue", "red"]
REPORTED = ["red", None, "blue"]
for actual, report in zip(ACTUAL, REPORTED):
    print("Actual:", actual, "Reported:", report)
    print("Pause and inspect" if report is None else "Report needs checking")
observation.expected: One missing report and one wrong report. A label alone does not establish the actual object.

sequence.code:
PROGRAM = [{"op": "log", "message": "Ready"},
           {"op": "ev3", "command": "eject"},
           {"op": "ev3", "command": "left_end"},
           {"op": "log", "message": "Inspect the stopped pickup fixture"}]
print("SIMULATION instructions; no hardware command sent")
for row in PROGRAM:
    print(row)
sequence.expected: Ready, simulated dispense, belt to endpoint, inspection. A printed command is not measured arrival.

FOLLOWER_START = 30
LEADER_NOW = 15

print("Absolute prediction:", LEADER_NOW, "degrees")

failure.code:
REPORTS = ["present", None, "present"]
completed = 0
for report in REPORTS:
    if report is None:
        print("STOP: missing observation; inspect before retry")
        break
    completed += 1
print("Simulated inspected objects:", completed)
failure.expected: Stop at the missing observation; one simulated inspected object.

extension.code:
from workshop import Factory, SimBelt, SimCamera, SimRobot
OBJECTS = ["red", "blue", "red", "unknown", "blue"]
RULES = {"red": "left", "blue": "right"}
factory = Factory(SimBelt(), SimCamera(OBJECTS), SimRobot())
for _ in OBJECTS:
    factory.one_cycle(RULES)
print(factory.counts)
print("SIMULATION routes:", factory.robot.actions)
assert sum(factory.counts.values()) == len(OBJECTS)

for destination, count in factory.counts.items():
    print(destination, ":", count)
print("Total objects:", sum(factory.counts.values()))

fixed_pick_place.code:
from workshop.blockly_client import Program, simulate_program
program = (Program().ev3("eject").ev3("left_end")
           .pick_place_recording("fixed_pick_place", .5))
result = simulate_program(program)
skill = result["taught_skills"][0]
print("Synthetic fixed-fixture rehearsal:", skill["state"])
print("Physical evidence:", skill["physical_evidence"])
assert skill["physical_evidence"] is False
assert not any(skill[k] for k in ("pickup_verified", "lift_verified", "release_verified"))
fixed_pick_place.expected: Explicit synthetic simulation only. Physical evidence and pickup/lift/release verification remain false.
